column6: Text
How can one enjoy meditation when one's knees are on fire?
The monks at Winchester Cathedral used props during long chanting sessions.
Thank you for this morning's talk on the recollections and faith. Could you elaborate on your point about faith and anāgamī? Has anyone been fully liberated through faith?
Faith is the trigger for letting go and relinquishment.
MN 52: Delight in the Dhamma and the third stage of liberation.
Would you kindly comment on the cultivation and use in one's Dhamma practice of one's creative gifts, such as music, art, dance, writing, and so on?
Master Hua disapproves of Rev. Heng Sure giving his instruments away.

I've realized that I'm like a fish in aversive water and was bringing that into practice, constantly rejecting what was happening and generally losing track of my meditation object, the breath. Can you speak a bit more about attitude versus object?
I have very little faith in the possibility of being enlightened in this lifetime; perhaps stream entry. Is stream entry a realistic possibility for many of us if leading householder lives?
SN 55.1: Unshakeable confidence and being established in virtue.
[The Island Chapters 16-19](The Island p. 279).
Is it permissible to take notes during your talks?

Can you speak about the balance between implementing an antidote to a hindrance and practicing patience? I'm having a lot of aversion, and as I try to use both of these practices I'm finding myself full of doubt and confusion.
Is the concept of anatta or no-self a suitable object of meditation?
What's the difference between proliferation and directed thought?
What are the characteristics/attainments of the eight noble beings? Where are they described?
On retreat, is it skillful to try to memorize some of the chants?

Sometimes I experience what one of my teachers has called a multiple hindrance attack. For me this manifests as sloth and torpor and restlessness, feeling as if they are arising simultaneously. Sloth and torpor may be primary; I'm not sure. Any wise words?
Could you please say a little more about the fifth hindrance, doubt? Is it self-doubt or doubt of the Dhamma?

I keep getting overwhelmed by a variety of intense and unpleasant bodily sensations. I have been trying to keep my focus on more neutral places in the body, but I still find that keeping the concentration anywhere in the body amplifies the unpleasant feelings, and I can't settle into a place of ease.
The energy we invest in it is where the suffering actually lies. In the end, a body is just a body.
May I ask the whole Abhayagiri gang what is your favorite meditation object?
Is it true that having images of a certain animal around will make you likely to be that animal in your next life?
Do you ever work with the 'thin line' between sleep and waking, dreaming and lucidity? It seems like a powerful or useful fulcrum.

Can any teacher suggest that we should _not_ pursue states of jhāna? 'If they happen, great; if not don't worry.' In a room full of about 60 devoted meditators, it seems unlikely that any of us are achieving this type of absorption. If we were, then the chiming of the bowl would be disrupting many people's jhānic states of meditation. Is jhāna really quite rare?
Can you please speak about how one practices on the third path or what happens leading up to the third path attainment?
Can you share some ways to deal with pride when the ego influences feelings negatively?
AN 6.104: I-making and mine-making.

Could you please talk about the process of cutting the chain of Dependent Origination? With a more mature practice, can one cut the chain earlier among the different links? How does this take place experientially?
A pin pricking a balloon.|Ajahn Chah
Has anyone ever attained enlightenment while walking meditation? What are the pros and cons of walking meditation?
How does one develop compassion such that one harbors no ill-will even when bandits dismember you with a double-handed saw (MN 21.20)?
For the enlightened person, there's no choice but compassion.|Ajahn Mahā Boowa
Please explain upekkha, which is the last of the Brahmavihāras, Ten Perfections, and Seven Factors of Enlightenment. It sounds important.
Can you please speak about the differences between clear seeing and awareness? Does one precede the other?

I have a friend, a beloved aversive type, who has regular angry outbursts. I chalk it up to frustration, yet find myself floundering in how to respond. Should I try to practice metta and patience, limit my association? Any words would be appreciated.
What is the correct motivation and expectation for meditation?
I'm feeling spacious in my heart. it is pleasant, and then I get sleepy. Can you advise on how to cultivate interest in spaciousness?
Do you have any ghost story at Wat Pah Nanachat?
The mother of a girl killed in an accident dedicates merit with the wish that her daughter be reborn in the family. The girl's ghost haunts Wat Pah Nanachat.
How do you expand your concentration and awareness beyond the breath when other conditions arise?
The object of attention needs to be appropriate to the quality of mind. ... As the mind becomes more refined, we need to pay attention to a more refined object.
Can you talk about how different hand positions or mudras are used in meditation?
Eight Precepts illuminates the vanity within.' Could you offer some encouragements or reflections on the beauty of the Dhamma as a remedy?
Chanting Book p. 6: Recollection of the Dhamma.
Ajahn Khao's realization came from reflecting on rice.
Could you review again what the antidotes to the Five Hindrances are? Also, if one has not correctly identified the hindrance at the moment and uses the incorrect remedy, so what?
SN 46.51: Starving the hindrances.
Throwing dust into the wind (Dhp 125).
AN 7.61: Antidotes for sloth and torpor.
Late night news, sports, and a sleeping pill. Any suggestions how my mind is going to be affected in the long run?
What is the difference between abandoning personality view (sakkāya-diṭṭhi) and realizing anatta?
What is hasituppāda citta---consciousness producing mirth---that is the Buddha's smile?
MN 81; MN 83; AN 5.180: Examples of the Buddha's smile.
MN 12.58: "You might think that the jujube fruit was bigger in those days ..."
SN 17.5: A dung beetle gloats about his pile.

Thank you for teaching that listening to Dhamma is a spiritual practice, not just information download. When you opened your heart to Ajahn Chah, even though you couldn't understand his words, would you say that was a sort of Dhamma transmission directly from one heart to another?
As wild and woolly as some of my experiences have been in the practice, I was wondering if there's a place for wilder-ness along the path? What is crazy wisdom?
Some people thought Ajahn Tongrat was crazy.

Ajahn Utane's biography of Ajahn Tongrat. Ajahn Mudito translated this into Portuguese in 2019, and there is a [machine translation](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sljCNyotNKznRnHVjh031b-vpEEe1Vpr/view) from the Portuguese.
Ajahn Tongrat dies on the Dhamma seat.
Does the remembrance of mindfulness have to do with our kamma?

I've been experiencing and witnessing an incredible sadness. At times it is dormant; at times it seems all-consuming. I've done okay at staying present, questioning its nature, its benefits, its hindrances, its source. I haven't come up with a specific cause for this grief/sorrow. Do you have any suggestions for furthering my investigation working with sadness, and how I might someday send it on its way?
Viewed from any sane perspective, the human condition is pretty sad.

I remember reading that Ajahn Chah used to ask monastics to meditate in a charnel ground to alleviate lust. With no charnel ground at my disposal, how to work with this strong sensual desire in meditation?
What kind of suffering does a non-returner experience? What makes a non-returner become an arahant?
What was that onomatopoeic word you mentioned? What does it mean?
I understand that you recently read Ajahn Geoff's wonderful new book [Skill in Questions](Skill in Questions). Might you share an insight that struck a fresh cord in your heart?

It seems that the mind and body are unreliable, not good refuges, yet everything about the Buddha, Dhamma, and Saṅgha relies upon the mind training---refining, watching, letting go. It sounds like it still relies on the mind. What am I missing?
SN 15.1: "Bound by ignorance and obstructed by craving."
What are mind-conditioners (e.g. MN 44.13, MN 118.19)? Are they feelings, habits, or something else?

While doing walking meditation today, a pleasurable sensation started unfolding in my body. When my mind reacted, it vanished. When mindfulness was reestablished, it recurred. This time I tried to lean into and investigate, and it similarly fizzled. How should I skillfully work with this?

When meditation is strong, awareness automatically falls upon the object, and both melt away quickly. However, sometimes hindrances cloud the mind, and the mind wanders. Is it best to develop more concentration? I've been experimenting with breath sensations.
AN 4.170: In Conjunction.
What is the most skillful thing to do when we can feel that there are a lot of blockages around the various energy centers in our body?
Are the Dhamma talks being taped for CDs or audio downloads on the internet?
If Ajahn Pasanno could go back in time and give a word of advice to Ven. Pasanno on the day of his ordination, what would he say?
Could you explain the role of enjoyment within the context of taking food with the purpose of nourishment?
Kd 15.31: The Buddha allows toothwoods and explains that using toothwoods makes you enjoy your food.
Can you review the 16 steps of mindfulness of breathing (MN 118.15)?
I often find myself wondering if it is equanimity or indifference I'm experiencing. Could you please enlighten me?

Is there a chant or a few lines that you can suggest to provide a smooth transitional bridge from chanting something such as Salutation to the Triple Gem (Chanting Book p. 9) into meditating on the breath? I feel disconnected: inspired by the meaning of the chant and then suddenly I'm focusing on my breath. Did the Buddha have a few powerful verses reminding us of the power of breath meditation?
MN 118.15: 16 steps of mindfulness of breathing; Chanting Book p. 85 has both Pāli and English.
Are transitions from stream entry to once-returner and once-returner to non-returner subtle or are there strong insight experiences? Will one be able to tell if he or she has moved to the next stage?
If weeping starts to happen while sitting, is it best to leave the hall or okay if some sound happens while in the group?
I've been feeling a large space/awareness in my body and in my head. I feel the outline of my form. What is a skillful way to deepen this place?

Can you elaborate on how to bring practice within the daily life setting? Even here, I feel I can walk around within my own bubble with my attention mostly focused inwardly. Can you describe how practice works when attention needs to be engaged in the fast-paced external world?

Can you recommend any particular books which share the teachings of the Buddha in more user-friendly ways---'Dhamma for Dummies'? I found the readings from the discourses/Canon repetitive and hard to relate to, yet you share so many Dhamma tidbits that are captivating and memorable.
_Eight Mindful Steps to Happiness_ by Bhante Gunaratana (commercial).
_In the Buddha's Words_ by Bhikkhu Bodhi (commercial).
[Life of the Buddha]().
What to do when the meditation practice seems dry and barren, a tedious, joyless exercise?
Ajahn Chah tries to make the practice even by walking for two hours, sitting for two hours, lying for two hours, and standing for two hours (Collected Teachings p. 29).
Can a person be enlightened without ever sitting? Or without ever hearing the Dhamma? Was anyone ever enlightened before the Buddha?
"Chickens sit for a long period of time, and they don't get very far."|Ajahn Chah
When Ajahn Chah sat meditation, it was like seeing a mountain sitting there.
SN 15.1: "Bound by ignorance and obstructed by craving."
A question in Thai asking for an explanation of hiri-otappa.
Could you speak about the subtle ringing in the ear known as the sound of silence as a meditation object, both on its own and in conjunction with ānāpānasati?

I have had more of a pedestrian view of the Dhamma, and for the first time I'm having trouble even referring to the Buddha as 'the Lord' (Chanting Book p. 23). Can you review taking refuge in the Buddha? Likewise, who is Lord Sahampati in the chant of requesting a Dhamma talk (Chanting Book p. 124)?
MN 26.20: The Brahma Sahampati invites the Buddha to teach.
I've noticed that my heart is really open in the evenings. Will you lead us in a metta meditation one of these evenings?
I'm a morning person.
Are we born with a sense of self or is this delusion seeded and cultivated by the world around us? If a child was raised being taught non-self and non-identity, how would they turn out?
What does it mean, 'When a monk breathes in, he satisfies the mind' (MN 118.20)?
It's a lot more fruitful than 'I'm a serious meditator and I'm skilled at making myself miserable!'

At times the breath becomes very subtle, almost imperceptible. I try to focus on the still point, but don't seem to be able to absorb. No lights have yet appeared. The space is quite pleasant, but eventually the refinement seems to dissipate and fade. Anything else to 'do?'
Any suggestions for calming the breath/body when its mind is set on racing?
Was Ajahn Chah an arahant? How can one tell when someone's work is done? Also, is it inappropriate to ask one's teacher if they are a stream enterer, once-returner, etc.?
To me, I'm more like a tree that birds can come and feed in. ... [What they say] I am is just the chattering of the birds.|Ajahn Chah
AN 4.192: Discerning another person's wisdom.
of mistaken estimates of enlightenment.

As I finished one length of my walking path, I realized that I was not the same person as when I started, that I was making myself each moment based on choices I made. How do I develop or at least remember this so I don't fall back into habitual patterns? It seems like each morning I have to rebuild my awareness.
Before my Dhamma eye opened, all I could see was macro-suffering. But now I can see nano-suffering on a massive scale. Sometimes I don't want to look. Any words of advice or encouragement?
"You've got dog shit in your bag, so it stinks everywhere you go."|Ajahn Chah

How should a stream enterer skillfully deal with delusional others, especially when it comes to family members? I feel like things can get really weird when the view of a stream enterer is so different from the rest.
What is the proper hand position while bowing? I see many various positions in the laypeople and some variation in the monastics.
Positioning the hands of a corpse.|Ajahn Chah
Please share thoughts on how to bring home and develop ways to be a better spouse and father. What from the practice might help the most towards kindness, generosity, and being present?
Have the patience to give others time.
I heard in your [ghost story](excerpt:TG2011_S03_F02) about dedicating merit. How do I do this? I would like to improve the kamma of my mother and little brother.

Can you speak more about perception? Confusion arises when I see perception and also see that the perception is accurate to what has occurred, that is the other person was disregarding, attacking, etc. So not only my memory, I also see identifying dukkha. Can you speak to this?
Did anyone ever need a knee replacement as a result of being on retreat? Is it okay to set up a few more chairs? Metta to knees everywhere.

I get great satisfaction from learning new skills and subjects. However, I get easily immersed, finely focused, and no mindfulness. Sometimes I take refuge in this state as it helps me sweep aside what I would rather not face. Can you offer any advice? Also, are there investigations I might pursue during retreat that may be helpful? P. S. I hear that 'accomplished in learning and craftsman's skills' is a higher blessing (Chanting Book p. 47).
So that glass of wine at dinner is going to eliminate my chances of stream entry? How about moderation in all things?
Would you please explain the concept of a Bodhisattva, a largely Mahāyāna teaching in the Theravāda tradition?
Somdet Toh waits for a dog sleeping on his robe to wake up.

Could you please talk about Shakyamuni Buddha, whose teaching we learn, and the ones before him, and the one to come Maitreya? Are the teachings the same? What is important for us to know about the Buddhas?
Chanting Book V2 p. 54: The Twenty-Eight Buddhas' Protection.
Ajahn Chah had tremendous lovingkindness, and because of that he had many, many people coming to him all the time. I'm going to focus on equanimity.|Ajahn Liem
Is it atta that carries kamma? Is it atta that takes a rebirth? How can we talk about atta?

Did you know Ajahn Paññāvaḍḍho? I saw the DVD about him that Abhayagiri offers and listened to some of his Dhamma talks and was touched by how gentle he seemed. Is it true that a rainbow appeared during the cremation of his body?

Can you offer some inspiration to the group as to observing the Eight Precepts on the Uposatha Days? I've been observing every quarter moon, and it would be comforting to know that I'm part of a larger group. Please reflect on the value of restraint outside the retreat environment.
Ajahn Pasanno's first Uposatha Day at Wat Pah Pong.
AN 8.41: "Suppose the lay people spent a day and a night living like the arahants."

Did you say in a previous Q&A that only through Buddhadhamma can one become liberated? No one in any other wisdom/spiritual tradition? While I am profoundly grateful to the Triple Gem, it seems dangerously fundamentalist to assume there is no other path possible. Is it so?
How does one use the kasiṇa and nimitta in meditation?
How does one overcome the threefold conceit (māna)? By seeing anicca and anatta in both self and other?
Any tips for stirring up the energy (viriya) that fuels Right Effort when coffee isn't enough?

Is the Deathless element, the knowing as Ajahn Chah called it, and rigpa as the Tibetans call it the same thing? And how is that different from the fifth khanda, consciousness? How can one practice with seeing the grasping of that khandha in meditation?

The quality of breath can change to very light, creating some pleasant changes like pain control. To what extent can breath be manipulated? Doesn't pure awareness act as an agent of change as well? What is the difference? Is the the source of self-healing?
A 102-year-old monk falls in the bathroom then completely heals his head injury in one day.
Most of the time I feel like a duck in a world full of chickens. Any advice on techniques to prevent the urge to compare myself to others would be greatly appreciated.
Why aren't the ducks more like chickens?|Ajahn Chah
What's the difference between mental formations and perception? I'm confused.
Can you give us a short bio on each of you please?
Ajahn Yatiko is on his way to Tibet, but two Thai men in a restaurant persuade him to visit Wat Pah Pong.
Bhante Suddhaso finds his way to Abhayagiri through Zen.
Ajahn Karuṇadhammo ordains at Abhayagiri after many years of lay practice.
Anagārika Jordan (now Ajahn Sudhīro) learns about Buddhism in college and has just taken up anagārika training at Abhayagiri.
Debbie Stamp travels in Asia, hears a talk by Ajahn Buddhadāsa, spends ten months at Amaravati and Chithurst, then volunteers to help start Abhayagiri.
She's the mother of our monastery.
What are some practices to deal with ill-will going repetitively towards one object?
AN 5.161: Removing Resentment.
Chanting Book p. 41: Reflection on kamma.
If there's a solution to the problem, why create difficulty around it? And then if there's not a solution to the problem, why create difficulty around it?|Shantideva

I believe we all found Ajahn Yatiko's comment on true insight shattering our beliefs pretty intriguing. I'm fairly certain that I'm millions of miles away from true insight, but what about those meditative moments where you go, 'Oh! I've never thought about that before, but how true.'? Are these possibly akin to true insight?
I'm confused about the distinctions between the third and fourth [Foundations of Mindfulness]. It seems like there's overlap. Some teachers put the hindrances under phenomena. Can you explain please?
MN 10.34-35: Mindfulness of mind.
Different translations of dhammānupassī, the fourth Foundation of Mindfulness.

A small window of anatta has opened. It is very fresh, light, and breezy, but the opening is small, and the rest of the window is caked with so much dirt and grime. I'm fearful that outside of the support of retreat, it could close. Even now it feels like it is opening and closing. How to best proceed?
The best thing is not claiming ownership over that insight. ... Pay attention to the feeling of it.
If you just stick your finger in the warm water, then you'll know what warm water is.|Ajahn Chah

I enjoyed the story of the healing green light used by the Thai venerable you shared with us [yesterday](excerpt:TG2011_S05_F26), and I also enjoyed the teachings of Ajahn Thate this morning. But then I'm wondering if the very act of trying to 'heal this body' or 'clarify and brighten this mind' acts to pull the heart out of neutral and into the world of grasping and desire. Could you please clarify this?
DN 16.2.23: The Buddha heals his illness.
The crux of it is how to live with non-clinging as the foundation.

Please explain enjoying a pleasant meditation versus hanging out blissfully with an angelic face. At what point should a calm mind switch to insight practice, and when do you use the term awareness or mindfulness practice?

While sitting in the dining hall, the image of a square cushion dropping away from my solar plexus occured. That brought the insight that I was neither inferior nor superior to others, as ego asserts, but we're all equal.
Friends and relatives in old age, sickness and death.|a common way to begin a Dhamma talk in Thailand
In order to avoid any unpleasant feelings, I tend to be among the first ones in the food line. I don't really feel good about it, but I can't help it. Any suggestions would be appreciated.
Path of Purification p. 39-40: Sāriputta goes against his desires regarding almsfood.
Ajahn Pasanno and vegetarian food at Wat Pah Pong.
How do Tibetan monks generate so much body heat to melt snow? I'd like to learn that and warm up this sometimes quite cold hall at night.
Ajahn Supah goes wandering through India, Tibet, and China. He described the Himalayas as cold.
What's the relationship between a deep insight experience (what's called kensho in Zen) and stream entry?

Hypothetically, a meditator through practice gains an experiential understanding of the Four Noble Truths and is established in mindfulness and equanimity. Life is good, and the glass is half full. However, there isn't a belief in rebirth and that suffering will end in this lifetime. Why should the meditator continue of the path?
Chanting Book p. 6: Opanayiko: Leading inwards/onwards.

For several months now, I've been trying not to get caught up in stories and just focus on the feelings. Every time I stop the story, the feeling seems to consistently stop as well, and I can no longer focus on it. What am I missing?
What is the Pāli word meaning not-made-of-that, non-fashioning, non-proliferation?

"Thank you for developing the wisdom to teach and the compassion to choose to teach. I trust we give you the opportunity to deepen your practice, especially of compassion and patience. The Buddha would be proud of you and your decision to teach instead of living in that nice little cave in a beautiful forest all peaceful and still. With metta."---us sentient beings.
"It was actually Ajahn Chah who made me teach."
Could you speak about the importance of intention and volition as related to karma and to the story about the chicken who set the intention to lay on her eggs but didn't follow through (SN 22.101)?
AN 6.63.33: Karma is volition.
Are desire and craving interchangeable, the same thing? Can craving or desire exist without suffering?
What did the Buddha say about giving all your assets away?
AN 5.41; AN 8.54; DN 31.26: Balanced living for householders.
Money for a monk is like having wings to fly.|Anonymous

Several years ago, I remember reading your little book [The Last Breath](The Last Breath) about your experience supporting a Thai Buddhist at the death chamber [in San Quentin Prison]. I was very impressed how someone who as facing the last hours of his life still had sati and clear consciousness, practiced generosity, requested food for the monks, and was humble and kind. Would you mind telling us about Jay's mindfulness again?
Jay offers Ajahn Pasanno a meal in prison and makes sure that his family and the guards have an opportunity to hear Dhamma.
Jay pays his last respects to Ajahn Pasanno.

Lately I've got more involved in fighting for social justice, especially with the Occupied Movement. It seems important in light of how messed up or system is. However, I'm finding it very difficult to keep any mindfulness or peace of mind, especially when menaced by police. Any suggestions?
Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro lead meditation at the Occupy Wall Street demonstration in London.
Can you please tell us about dreams? Do they reveal our defilements? Do you have any interesting dream stories?
Two Western monks ask Ajahn Chah at what point he became confident that he would have a major realization. Ajahn Chah describes three dreams in response.
Stillness Flowing p. 111-113.

Did I understand correctly that thought is saṅkhāra, which is distinct because of volition? It is clear that some thought is volitional, but what about the many random, crazy thoughts that arise unbidden?
How much karma is carried in thought? I've been observing what feels like the result of past unmindful thought. Is the karmic charge neutralized through mindful awareness of unwholesome thought?
Do neutral feelings equal equanimity?
Do you have any news you can share about the relationship between Ajahn Brahm and the rest of the saṅgha in the Ajahn Chah lineage? I heard that he was going to meet with some elder monks in England.

Ajahn Karuṇadhammo's talk truly resonated with me. While years of breath practice has yielded only a few, albeit very important, experiences of concentration, I've grown more and more clear about the depths of my defilements and the programs that run through my brain. (Wow! I'm neurotic.) I'm feeling a bit hopeless, but can this possibly be good? Rather than an object and trying for concentration, should I focus on something else for a while until I've developed skillful means? Is it possible that one's kamma is such that deep concentration is unlikely or that the background mind can be too aversive for concentration? I really need some anatta here, don't I?
Is it skillful to dig up sensual thoughts and contemplate the ugly side of it during vipassanā?
I'd like to swap the order of precepts around when it gets dull. Is it a waste of effort?

Today I saw a milk carton being thrown away. I'm not sure if everyone knows they are recyclable. This sight initiated a fire for me. I told myself, 'It's just thrown away.' Then I told myself, 'It's just my mind on fire.' Can you speak about Right View? Does it come back to what I can truly know? How do I consider long-term patterns that may not be apparent right away? One milk carton is not a big deal. One milk carton a day starts to add up.
We can be right and still create tremendous suffering.
When I return to the world of speaking again, what would be a good quick mental check-in that I could use before I open my mouth and possibly make a mess of things? Any tips for Right Speech?
MN 58.8: True, timely, and beneficial.
"Don't bring up these issues before the meal."|Ajahn Chah
Can brightness of mind and fatigue coexist? Is mental fatigue a defilement?
Ajahn Pasanno felt mental fatigue while preparing for Ajahn Chah's cremation yet had a bright mind.
[Ajahn Karuṇadhammo's] reflection on the parts of the body and the whole body helped me contemplate and relinquish. Is it possible to read that reflection somewhere? Will it be on the CD?

Could the summary of this week's rich teachings be represented graphically? For some people, it is helpful to see the flow of a process visually, including all the players, interactions, and scenarios. There are so many details in the chain of events that it's easy to miss one.

Meditation is work. Sometimes I'm very tired, can't think, can't hear, can't sit, can't sleep; I just show up and breathe. How are you doing? What keeps you going? I'm so touched with your generous presence, patience, and deep commitment.
There's only two things you need to do in Dhamma practice: know and let go.|Ajahn Chah
What is the position of the monastics in relation to the lay community? Are we viewed as essentially impure and filled with defilements? I read that somewhere.

Which is more powerful: lovingkindness or knowledge of suffering? It seems that our noble silence and internal mindfulness put the retreatants in the mode of not making eye contact, not sharing a smile. Isn't there room to be mindful of our Dhamma friends, even if we don't really know most of them by offering a smile? Am I too concerned with other people's actions? Meditation is serious business.

I'm having alternating intense periods of spaciousness and intense periods of agitation and sleepiness. Can you speak to this? I seem to identify very strongly with both states. It takes some time before I see the dukkha. I feel a bit hopeless about identification and the possibility of relinquishing it or even getting some relief from it. Any guidance would be appreciated.
A gardener's duty is to prepare the soil and protect the tree. The fruit appears according to the nature of the tree.|Ajahn Chah

Is the experience of Nibbāna (that is the cessation of all formations) the same for a stream enterer, once-returner, etc., or does the experience manifest differently depending on the level of realization? Do the suttas or commentaries touch on this subject? Any stories from the Forest Tradition related to it?

How do the Thais, and especially Buddhist practitioners, perceive the flooding disasters in Thailand? Is it just an unfortunate chain of effects due to bad weather, and that is how it is, so neutral, no feelings?
You mean all I have to do is drop dukkha from the mind? Why didn't you tell me that years ago?
Is atammayatā like nippapañca (non-proliferation)?
Would an opposite of dukkha be contentment not dependent on conditioning?
Would you say Nibbāna is a constant, conscious choice, creation, which is ultimately easier than creating dukkha?
Someone who is freed wouldn't be able to kill an ant no matter how you enticed or coerced them.|Ajahn Chah
Do you have any ideas or feelings on the question, 'Who created life?' Did Buddha know how it all began?
AN 4.77: Inconceivable Matters.

If this body is elemental and sustained by some force of nature, no self present, why do we have individual senses of 'I am witnessing'? Kamma? So when we all become enlightened and end the cycle of rebirth (I'm hoping for tomorrow noon-ish) then what?
There's a practical usefulness in having I and other people.|Ajahn Chah
Collected Teachings p. 23.
After his enlightenment, did the Buddha ever feel anger or sadness? Were those entries wiped from his program?
